en: Buddhavamsa 25.
The Lineage of Buddha Koṇāgamana:
"After Kakusandha..."
The perfectly awakened one, supreme among bipeds,
the Victor named Koṇāgamana,
the eldest in the world, the bull among men.
Having fulfilled ten qualities,
he has crossed over the wilderness;
having washed away all impurity, he has transcended the realm of Māra.
He attained supreme enlightenment while the Leader Koṇāgamana was setting in motion the Wheel of Dhamma.
There was the first realization for thirty thousand koṭis;
and while he was performing the miracle,
In the crushing of the arguments of opponents,
there was a second realization for twenty thousand times ten million beings.
Then, having performed a miraculous transformation,
the Conqueror went to the city of the gods;
there the Fully Awakened One dwelt.
While teaching the seven books on the Paṇḍukambala stone slab,
that Sage dwelt there for the rains retreat.
There was a third realization for ten thousand times ten million [beings] under that God of Gods as well.
There was a single gathering of those whose taints were destroyed, who were stainless,
whose minds were peaceful, and who were steadfast.
At that time, there was a gathering of thirty thousand bhikkhus who had transcended the floods.
And when they were broken by death,
at that time I was a kṣatriya named Pabbata.
Endowed with friends and ministers,
possessing infinite strength and transport,
he went to see the Fully Enlightened One.
Having heard the unsurpassed Dhamma,
he invited the Saṅgha together with the Buddha and gave them whatever gifts they desired.
Fine cotton cloth, Chinese silk,
silk from the kośa tree,
and woolen blankets; even golden sandals—
I gave [alms] to the Teacher’s disciples.
That Buddha, sitting in the midst of the Saṅgha, also made a prediction concerning me:
“In this auspicious aeon,
this one will become a Buddha.
There was a delightful city called Kapila;”
we shall be face to face with this one.
Having heard her words as well, [he said:]
I further clarified my mind;
I resolved upon a higher vow for the fulfillment of the ten perfections.
Seeking omniscience,
having given a gift to the Supreme among Men,
I renounced my great sovereignty.
I went forth in the presence of the Victor.
There was a city named Sobhavatī,
and the kshatriya there was named Sobha.
In that city dwelt a great family of the Fully Enlightened One;
there was also a brahmin named Yaññadatta.
He was the father of the Buddha;
the mother of the Teacher Koṇāgamana was named Uttarā.
For three thousand years he dwelt in the household life; contented,
well-pleased, and thoroughly satisfied, he remained in the Tusita heaven.
There were three supreme palaces,
and sixteen thousand women fully adorned.
A woman named Rucigattā and a son named Satthavāha;
having seen four omens, [he departed].
He departed by elephant-vehicle;
for six months, the Supreme Person practiced the course of striving on foot.
Being entreated by Brahmā,
the Great Hero, the Leader Koṇāgamana, set the Wheel of Dhamma in motion.
In the Deer Park, the Supreme among Men had two chief disciples named Bhīyyasa and Uttara.
The attendant named Sotthija was the one for the Teacher Koṇāgamana.
And [the island] Uttara Samudda...
were his chief female disciples;
the Bodhi tree of that Blessed One is called the Udumbara.
Ugga and Somadeva were the foremost attendants;
as were Sīvalā and Sāmā.
They were his foremost attendants.
In height, that Buddha was thirty cubits tall.
Just as a conch shell at the mouth of a furnace,
so was he adorned with rays of light for thirty thousand years.
Such was the lifespan of the Buddha;
remaining for that long,
he delivered many people across.
Having raised up a monument of Dhamma,
adorned with the robe of Dhamma,
and having fashioned a bouquet of Dhamma flowers—
He has attained Nibbāna along with his disciples.
His followers are of great splendor,
proclaiming the glorious Dhamma.
All that has vanished;
are not all conditioned things empty?
Thus spoke the Sambuddha Koṇāgamana.
He attained final Nibbāna in a mountain monastery;
his relics were widely distributed throughout various regions.
The twenty-third lineage is that of the Blessed One Koṇāgamana.
